headline: The bill market now prices hikes, not cuts — 3m at 4.30 versus 3.88 funds, and today's 17bp 2-year shock broke the one thing still working: the rotation.
summary: Yesterday's story was gold losing $4,000. Today's is bigger and upstream of it: the front end repriced to a Fed that hikes. The 3-month bill is 4.30, at the 100th percentile of its year and 42bp above the 3.88 effective funds rate; the 2-year jumped 17bp to 4.73, the 5-year 14bp to 4.81, the 10-year 10bp to 4.98 and the 30-year to 5.35. 2s10s flattened another basis point to 24bp, the 7th percentile of the year, with T10Y2Y z=-1.10. Crucially this is not a growth scare: 5-year breakevens rose 6bp to 2.31 and 10-year to 2.24 alongside Brent +3.3% to 95.78 and WTI +2.6% to 88.78. Real yields did the damage — DFII10 +12bp to 2.78, sitting 24.2% above its 200-day. Core CPI is turning up at z=0.93 with the index at the 100th percentile, and MOVE is +6.5% to 98.4, +42% in three months. The rates composite at -40 is the single worst reading on the board.

The S&P only lost 0.4% and the Nasdaq 0.3%, which flatters the day. The damage is beneath: Russell 2000 -1.7%, IWM/SPY -1.3%, MDY -1.2%, and RSP/SPY -0.5% after stretching to z=3.10. The breadth trade that absorbed the AI unwind for a month is itself now rolling. Everything funded by the back end got hit in one print: gold -2.9% to 3,884.5 (0th percentile, 13.4% below its 200-day), silver -3.6%, GDX -4.0%, GDXJ -4.7%, NEM -4.9%, bitcoin -3.5% to 71,379, IBIT -4.5%, MSTR -6.5%, COIN at the 0th percentile of its 52-week range, ITB -1.8% and XHB -1.7% after a +10.8%/+7.1% month built on a 29bp mortgage decline that just reversed. VIX +6.9% to 18.70 with VIX/VIX3M back to 0.932 and turning up. DXY is 103.17 at the 100th percentile, EURUSD 1.1051 at the 0th, USDCHF at the 100th — the dollar is the transmission mechanism and it is maxed.

Index-level credit stayed calm — HY OAS -4bp to 3.30, IG -1bp to 0.90, BBB -1bp, HYG/IEF +0.3%, BKLN at the 97.5th percentile — but the tail is paying for it. CCC spreads blew out another 19bp to 13.30, now +77bp on the month, +445bp year-to-date, and at the 95th percentile. That split (IG tightening, CCC decompressing) plus small caps underperforming on a 17bp 2-year move is the clean signal of a funding-cost problem, not a solvency problem — for now. Liquidity offers no cushion: bank reserves -2.3% on the month and rolling over, net liquidity -0.4%, RRP at $0.25bn.

What is genuinely good: the economy. Claims 200k, continuing claims 1.697m at the 1st percentile, unemployment 4.1% and falling, JOLTS 7,523 and +4.6%, industrial production +0.63, capacity utilization at the 100th percentile. Energy is the one commodity turning up with XLE +1.5%, XOM +1.8%, XOP +1.6% and natural gas +4.5%. Europe and India keep working — DAX +1.2% at the 100th percentile, CAC z=1.37, Sensex +13.8% on the month at z=3.35, INDA RS +12.1%. And the chip tape, for all of today's NVDA -4.3%, is up violently on the week: SOXX +17.5%, AVGO +25.0%, AMD +44.7%, MU +21.6%. That dispersion — NVDA at the 1.9th percentile of its year, 18.5% below its 200-day, while AMD sits 39.4% above its own — is the most extreme single relationship on the board.

good.text: Index credit refused to crack on a 17bp 2-year move: HY OAS -4bp to 3.30, IG -1bp to 0.90, BBB -1bp, HYG/IEF +0.3% and turning up, BKLN at the 97.5th percentile of its year.

The labor and output data are not rolling: claims 200k, continuing claims 1.697m at the 1st percentile, unemployment 4.1% and down 30bp y/y, JOLTS 7,523 (+4.6%), industrial production +0.63, capacity utilization at a 52-week high.
Energy is the one commodity complex turning up into the rate shock: Brent +3.3% to 95.78, WTI +2.6%, natgas +4.5%, XLE +1.5%, XOP +1.6%, XOM +1.8%, CVX +1.4% — all with XLE 9.5% above its 200-day.

Non-US leadership is real and it is Europe plus India: DAX +1.2% at the 100th percentile, CAC +0.7% (z=1.37), Euro Stoxx +1.0%, Sensex +13.8% on the month at z=3.35 with acceleration +3.11, INDA +9.1% and 12.1% ahead of the S&P.
The chip snapback is still intact under one bad day: SOXX +17.5% on the week, AVGO +5.5% today and +25.0% on the week, AMD +5.9%/+44.7%, MU +21.6%, TAIEX +3.6% and KOSPI +2.6%.
Defensive and cash-flow leadership keeps absorbing flow: XLV +10.7% on the month at z=2.50 and the 96th percentile, LLY +22.4%, COST +14.6%, HD +18.5%, WMT +12.4%, SPLV z=1.92.

bad.text: A hike is being priced, not a cut: 3-month bill 4.30 at the 100th percentile and 42bp above 3.88 effective funds; 2-year +17bp to 4.73, 5-year +14bp, 10-year 4.98, 30-year 5.35, MOVE +6.5% to 98.4 (+42% in 3 months).

The move is real-yield-led and inflation-confirmed, the worst mix for duration: 10y TIPS +12bp to 2.78 and 24.2% above its 200-day, 5y breakevens +6bp to 2.31, core CPI turning up at z=0.93 with the index at the 100th percentile.
CCC spreads decompressed 19bp to 13.30 — +77bp on the month, +445bp YTD, 95th percentile — while IG and BBB tightened. The tail is paying the funding bill alone.
The breadth bid that absorbed the AI unwind is cracking: RSP/SPY -0.5% off a z=3.10 extension, IWM/SPY -1.3%, Russell 2000 -1.7%, MDY -1.2%, XRT -1.8%, ITB -1.8% — nothing left to rotate into.

Dollar wrecking ball at the 100th percentile: DXY 103.17, EURUSD 1.1051 at the 0th percentile, USDCHF at the 100th, CEW -0.6%, EEM -1.5%, EEM/SPY -4.4% on the month; USDBRL still z=3.42 with acceleration +2.79 and EWZ -25.9% on the month.

Everything funded off the back end got liquidated at once: gold -2.9% at the 0th percentile, silver -3.6%, GDXJ -4.7%, NEM -4.9%, BTC -3.5% to 71,379, IBIT -4.5%, MSTR -6.5%, COIN at the 0th percentile. VIX +6.9% with the term structure at 0.932 and turning up.

trades.name: Short long duration into a hiking repricing
trades.line: Short TLT: 2y +17bp, bills at 4.30, breakevens rising with oil
trades.expr: Short TLT outright, or buy Jan TLT 78 puts; pair against a small IEF short if you want pure duration with less convexity.
trades.thesis: The curve is repricing a Fed that hikes again, not cuts. The 3-month bill at 4.30 is 42bp above effective funds at 3.88, core CPI is turning up (z=0.93, index at the 100th percentile) and the move is led by real yields (DFII10 2.78, 24.2% above its 200-day) with breakevens rising alongside Brent, not falling. TLT's +2.2% one-month bounce was built on a 26bp 10-year rally that has now been given back in a week.
trades.trigger: 2-year +17bp to 4.73 today, 5-year +14bp, 10-year +10bp to 4.98, 30-year 5.35, MOVE +6.5% to 98.4, 5y breakeven +6bp to 2.31 with Brent +3.3%.
trades.stop: 10-year back under 4.75 with breakevens falling (a genuine growth scare), or claims breaking above 230k; on the position, TLT +4%.

trades.name: Long oil equities vs short gold miners
trades.line: Long XOP / short GDX: oil +3%, gold at the 0th percentile
trades.expr: Long XOP, short GDX, dollar-neutral 1:1. Add XOM as a lower-beta substitute for half the long if you want less E&P torque.
trades.thesis: A rising-real-yield, strong-dollar world is poison for non-yielding metals and a tailwind for cash-generating energy. Gold is 13.4% below its 200-day at the 0th percentile of its year with miners still priced for $4,000+; crude is turning up with oil/gold +5.7% today and +24.3% over three months, and XLE's relative strength vs the S&P is +8.6% over three months.
trades.trigger: Brent +3.3% to 95.78 and WTI +2.6% while gold -2.9%, silver -3.6%, GDX -4.0% and GDXJ -4.7%; OIL_AU +5.7% in a single session, DFII10 2.78.
trades.stop: Brent back under 88 or the 10-year real yield under 2.55 (which re-funds the gold trade); on the pair, -8%.
trades.target: +12% on the pair; XOP toward 205 with GDX toward 74.

trades.name: Short the crypto-equity tail
trades.line: Short MSTR vs long IBIT: the premium unwinds faster than BTC
trades.expr: Short MSTR against a half-sized long in IBIT, so you own the premium compression rather than a naked bitcoin short.
trades.thesis: Crypto is the purest short-duration liquidity asset on the board and liquidity is tightening: bank reserves -2.3% on the month and rolling over, net liquidity -0.4%, a 3-month bill at the 100th percentile. MSTR is falling twice as fast as its own asset (-24.8% vs BTC -12.5% on the month), which is how a collapsing equity premium looks. COIN at the 0th percentile of its 52-week range confirms the equity complex, not just the coin, is being de-rated.
trades.trigger: BTC -3.5% to 71,379, IBIT -4.5%, MSTR -6.5% and COIN -4.1% today; ETH -16.6% and SOL -21.5% on the month with all four rolling over.
trades.stop: MSTR outperforms IBIT by 10% on any bitcoin bounce (premium re-expands), or the 2-year drops back below 4.50.

trades.name: Semis dispersion: buy the washed-out leader
trades.line: Long NVDA / short AMD: 1.9th vs 86th percentile, same industry
trades.expr: Long NVDA, short AMD, dollar-neutral. Alternatively long NVDA vs short SMH at 1:1 if you want the single-name risk out of the short leg.
trades.thesis: This is the most stretched intra-industry relationship on the board. NVDA is -27.3% on the month (z=-2.19), 18.5% below its 200-day, at the 1.9th percentile of its 52-week range and 25.3% behind the S&P over a month. AMD is +173% YTD, 39.4% above its 200-day, at the 86th percentile and just printed +44.7% in a week. Both sell the same end-demand. One of these two prices is wrong and the cheap one carries the index.
trades.trigger: NVDA -4.3% today while AMD +5.9% and AVGO +5.5%; SOXX +17.5% on the week with NVDA not participating — a liquidation signature, not a fundamental one.
trades.stop: NVDA loses another 8% relative to AMD, or NVDA closes below 150 (which makes it a fundamental story, not positioning).

trades.name: Low vol over small caps as the funding squeeze bites
trades.line: Long SPLV / short IWM: 17bp on the 2-year, CCC +19bp
trades.expr: Long SPLV, short IWM, 1:1. Cheaper variant: long USMV vs short IWM.
trades.thesis: Small caps are the most floating-rate-exposed part of the equity market, and the funding cost just reset higher while the CCC tail decompressed. The one-month small-cap squeeze (IWM/SPY z=1.13 with acceleration +1.87) is the trade that unwinds first when the front end moves. Low vol is doing the opposite — SPLV z=1.92, USMV at the 96.6th percentile.
trades.trigger: Russell 2000 -1.7% and IWM/SPY -1.3% today on a 17bp 2-year move; CCC OAS +19bp to 13.30 (+77bp on the month) while IG and BBB tightened; RSP/SPY finally turning lower off z=3.10.
trades.stop: The 2-year back under 4.50 with CCC spreads tightening 50bp, or -4% on the pair.

trades.name: Fade the homebuilder squeeze
trades.line: Short ITB: +10.8% month built on a mortgage drop now reversing
trades.expr: Short ITB outright, or buy Jan ITB puts ~5% out of the money. DHI is the single-name proxy if you prefer.
trades.thesis: Builders rallied 10.8% in a month purely on a 29bp mortgage decline to 7.11 — not on volumes. Housing starts are -5.2% and at the 11th percentile, permits at the 20th percentile, consumer sentiment 48.1 and falling. With the 10-year back at 4.98 and real yields at 2.78, the entire basis of that rally has reversed, and XHB/SPY at z=1.84 is still carrying the extension.
trades.trigger: ITB -1.8% and -4.9% on the week, XHB -1.7%, DHI -8.4% on the week, all while the 10-year added 10bp and the 2-year 17bp.
trades.stop: Mortgage rate breaks below 6.80 or a 10-year rally through 4.70; on the position, ITB +8%.

trades.name: Long India vs short Brazil in EM
trades.line: Long INDA / short EWZ: z=+2.0 vs z=-3.4, and BRL still breaking
trades.thesis: EM is splitting on currency, not growth. The Indian rupee is strengthening (USDINR -2.2% on the month, z=-2.18) while USDBRL is +12.0% on the month at z=3.42 with acceleration +2.79 — a funding accident still in progress. Sensex is +13.8% on the month (z=3.35) and turning up; Bovespa is -17.2% at z=-3.34 and EWZ -25.9% with no sign of a base.
trades.trigger: INDA +9.1% on the month and 12.1% ahead of the S&P, vs EWZ -2.0% today and 23.8% behind; CEW -0.6% confirms the EM currency drag is idiosyncratic to Latam, not broad.
trades.stop: USDBRL back below 5.35 (a real stabilisation) or -8% on the pair.
